title: Study Finds Public Evidence Gap for Pathology AI Devices
key_facts: A study published 5 Oct 2026 in npj Digital Medicine found public, device-specific performance evidence for 30 of 77 AI diagnostic software products in digital pathology and blood-cell analysis; none for the other 47.
The 77 devices from 29 manufacturers were CE-marked or FDA-authorized: 68 digital-pathology and nine hematology products.
The team was led by Diponkor Mondal of Helsinki University Hospital and the University of Helsinki.
It describes what researchers could locate publicly, not proof the devices were never validated.
ThePrint reported that 25 of the 30 evidence studies were retrospective, with a median of 211 patients, slides or specimens.
Only five devices had studies comparing pathologists with and without AI help.
The authors call for more consistent reporting and prospective multicentre assessment; two authors disclosed Cellbytes shareholdings.
quote_evidence: Researchers found none for the other 47.
This is a finding about what researchers could locate—not proof the devices were never validated.
why_it_matters_hint: Regulatory approval of pathology AI does not mean public evidence exists that it works in a given lab.
notes: Kenyan outlet's account of the npj Digital Medicine study, citing ThePrint for some numbers. Original paper not read.
